title: Widget, Element, Render Trees in Flutter

scenes.line1: Why does Flutter use three trees?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why Flutter uses not one, but three different trees to build your app? Let's break down what each tree does and why it matters.

scenes.label: Widget
scenes.sub: Describes the UI structure, like a blueprint.
scenes.say: First up, the widget tree. This is your user interface blueprint. It shows what widgets make up your screen.
Next, the element tree. This holds live widget instances and their state. Finally, the render tree handles layout and painting, making your app actually appear on screen.

scenes.title: See the trees in DevTools
scenes.say: You can use the Flutter DevTools inspector to actually see and debug all three trees in action.

scenes.question: Which tree handles painting?
scenes.right: Render tree. It controls layout and drawing.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: Don't confuse the widget tree with the render tree. Only the render tree handles layout and painting.
